params.brief: Main theme: a proud, weathered horn melody over lyre and frame drum; D dorian; the motif returns in the coronation cue.
Skarn home hall: hearth-warm aeolian lyre and bone flute, steady frame drum; fjord-cold but familiar.
Hvarn home hall: slow triple-time dorian with bowed strings and harp, forest-dark and stubborn.
Eyjar home hall: lilting compound-time mixolydian with flute and lyre, salt wind and island pride.
Sailing, calm seas: wide open drones, gently rocking 6/8, flute phrases far apart; the long whale-road.
Sailing, storm: driving string ostinato, war drums and horn calls; spray and danger, not despair.
Albrenn and Cael lands: harp and chant over drones, dorian, monastery stillness and green hills.
Corvaine: courtly mixolydian dance in three, fiddle and lyre, the confidence of horsemen.
Velkar river markets and Saraleon: phrygian oud and flute over a busy drum, wealth and old empire.
Mead-hall, rowdy (diegetic): fast jig-like fiddle and lyre with clapping; a hall band in full cry.
Mead-hall, lament (diegetic): a single hummed voice and lyre, late-night memory of the fallen.
Battle, shield wall: aeolian war drums and drone (low stem), string ostinato and choir (mid), horn calls and fiddle (high). Stems loop in sync.
low intensity stem of battle shieldwall; same length and tempo as the other stems.
mid intensity stem of battle shieldwall; same length and tempo as the other stems.
high intensity stem of battle shieldwall; same length and tempo as the other stems.
Battle, raid: fast phrygian assault; drums and drone (low), ostinato and choir (mid), horn, flute and driving slaps (high). Stems loop in sync.
low intensity stem of battle raid; same length and tempo as the other stems.
mid intensity stem of battle raid; same length and tempo as the other stems.
high intensity stem of battle raid; same length and tempo as the other stems.
Duel: heartbeat drums and a tense phrygian pedal; the fiddle enters as the fight intensifies.
Delve / mystery: cave reverb, sparse flute and harp over a low drone; wonder and unease without anything supernatural.
Allthing: dignified dorian procession with horn calls and steady drum; law spoken on the rock.
Funeral / epitaph: slow aeolian dirge, choir and horn, a single toll per bar.
Coronation / victory: the main-theme motif reborn in mixolydian with fanfare, choir and full drums.
New saga: a short, hopeful opening as a founder and homeland are chosen; the main-theme motif in waiting.
World map: broad and searching, horn and strings over a slow drum; the whole whale-road laid out.
Great hall: stately hearth-hall music for the jarl’s seat, lyre and strings with a measured drum.
Longhouse: homely and close, lyre and soft flute by the family fire.
Smithy: steady working rhythm, low strings and drum keeping time like a hammer.
Shipyard: busy and salt-bright, lilting lyre and flute over the craft of keel and strake.
Market: bustling trade music, oud-like plucking, flute and quick hand drums.
Mead-hall, warm (diegetic): a gentle hall band playing for friends; lyre and humming, cups and fire.
Battle at sea: rowing drums and driving strings, horn calls across the water; one full track, no stems.
Arrival: landfall at a new shore; wide strings and horn, wonder and wariness.
Expedition: planning a voyage; purposeful, rocking compound time with lyre and drone.
Victory: triumphant fanfare, choir and full drums after the battle is won.
Chronicle: reflective saga-telling music for reading the deeds of the house; lyre and voice.
Wedding: festive and tender, lyre, flute and clapping drum for a marriage feast.
Birth: soft and luminous, harp and humming for a child born to the house.
Settlement: steady building music for a growing steading; lyre, flute and drum.
Affairs of the realm: measured, thoughtful council music; strings and lyre over a quiet drum.
Omen read: phrygian choir cluster and high flute over a deep drum; an uneasy sign.
Birth in the family: rising harp arpeggio, flute and warm strings.
Death: falling horn line over choir and three slow drum strokes.
Victory: horn fanfare to the octave with drums and strings.
Defeat: falling strings and a low horn over a war-drum hit.
Relic found: shimmering harp ascent with choir; awe and weight of history.

Narrator: warm, wry, a little ironic; an old storyteller by the fire.
Skald: declaimed alliterative verse with kennings; measured, ringing, proud.
Hirdmaster: blunt, loyal, dry and practical; few words, low voice.
Steward: careful, precise, slightly anxious about the stores.
Seer: quiet, breathy, unhurried; speaks of omens as signs to be weighed.
The Rival: venomous wit, amused contempt.
Townsfolk and leaders: culture-specific; Albric formal-pious, Corvani courtly, Velkar mercantile-proud, Saraleonese imperial-bored.
